data.why: These are the project's own pytest fixtures: valid SpikeGLX .imro files and SpikeGLX-exported activity-survey .txt files for each supported probe family, matching exactly what the GUI's 'load .imro' and 'load survey overlay' file inputs expect.

goals: Select a Neuropixels probe type (1.0, 2.0 1-shank, 2.0 4-shank, Quadbase) and pick a built-in preset electrode layout
Interactively select or deselect individual electrodes while the GUI enforces electrode-ADC wiring constraints
Load a pre-existing .imro file to visualize or continue editing a probe's channel map
Overlay a SpikeGLX activity-survey (firing-rate-by-depth) file to guide electrode selection toward active recording sites
Overlay brain anatomy (region boundaries along each shank) to target specific anatomical structures
Export the finished selection as an .imro file for direct use in SpikeGLX

review.summary: The tree gets the core of PixelMap right: pick a probe, build a channel map that respects the wiring constraints by preset, typed ranges or drawing, guide it with an activity survey, then export the .imro/PDF/Kilosort files or a share link. The cited screens I opened back it up. It leaves out the anatomy guidance that the paper's title names and the reference/gain settings that the README says go into the file, and a few tasks are interface mechanics, so it needs those fixes before filing.
